chapter: Trumpet styles and early New Orleans scene
title: Playing with Freddie Keppard in Chicago; drummers Snags and Hilaire
summary: He recalls joining a Keppard band, naming its members, then discusses Chicago drummers.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Was there any of the guys playing like Freddie Caput down here?

Well, no. But I played with Freddie, you know. That's something I forgot to tell you. Now that was a trumpet player in the band. See, I went to that dream and there were so many different fellows, but now I went there with Freddie Caput. But how it happened, it wasn't tying the band to Freddie Caput band. Oh yeah. But I went there with him.
Who was in the band with Freddie?

He had some boys there, a light boy on tenor. And I'll tell you who he had with him. Lester Boone. You remember him? Yeah. Alco player, tenor player, something. Well he had him, and he had Felipe Trombo from here, Dutre, what's his name, Noda Dutre or something like that? Noda Dutre. Well he had him, and me, and himself, and he had a violin player named Clowns Lee. He was a good violin player, boy. He was a sweetheart. He played the devil out of the violin. And them the ones I can remember. I don't know if he had Snaggs on drum or not. That's the only drummer I remember. I played with a whole lot in Chicago with Snaggs. Francois, he played a drummer in that little band. I played with him with Snaggs, I played with him more than any drummer.
Well along the subject of drummers in Chicago, ever remember Andrew Hillier?
Sure I remember Andrew Good. Who was he with? He died, didn't he? Yeah. Yeah, we used to call him Hillier, yeah.

Well, I'm trying to think. I think he worked a whole lot with Dave Peyton. Yeah, he's up there along in that class, Dave Peyton. He worked a whole lot with Dave, I know. He worked a whole lot with Dave Peyton.
